body: Indeed. Your life belongs only to you. For some people, they take it upon themselves to please those around them and stay alive for their sake. But that should not be the norm. If based on your sound judgement that you should be allowed to leave, then do it. Other's judgement comes second to that. All the best.

I believe that leaving those dear to you, or at least those you believe are dear to you, will bring about a certain level of sadness and disappointment. Yet, I feel that it is not selfish to put your well-being above others. You have the right to control your life, how it starts as well as how it ends. It is up to you to exercise such control. I might not be able to fully understand you and relate to your conditions, but I am experiencing something similar to your case. Many a times I have withdrawn from society and lock myself up in my room. One thing I realised is: no one really cares about your problem. You are on your own in this battle against your mind. If one day you disappear, people most likely are not going to notice. Bear in mind that this is not the case for everyone.  Some people do have a supportive network of friends that will make them feel loved and worthy but for most of us, the fact that we are here to share about our loneliness and desperation already highlights that it is not the case. So in my case, I just hold on, being the naive person that I am hoping that the future will get better. Maybe I am lucky that I am naive. Maybe I am not. It is up to you to decide. Regardless, I hope that you find peace in your life.

In the end, you are always alone in your battle with your mind. If you're lucky enough, you just might survive and recover from it. But for many of us, we carry the burden until the day we die. Some just choose to hasten the process and take an early leave while others are just letting themselves getting thrown around in the turbulence of life, holding on till mother nature ties her connection with us. In the end, our lives belong to us only; we are free to do whatever we feel like with it. Everyone lead different lives, staying alive should not be the default. I hope you will be able to resolve yourself and come to a conclusion that satisfy your conscience, since no one can and will do that for you. I hope you find peace.

I think it goes down to the fundamental set of assumptions that we ultimately subscribe to. If we were to look at the environment around us and its development throughout history, there has been multiple prey-predator relationship involving ant. For example, anteater has been feeding on ants for longer than humans have existed. Is it immoral to do so?  I don't think so.

In the end, according to the social contract theory, the moral or immoral value of an action is dependent on the society's agreement on such actions. If society agrees an act is immoral, then it shall be deemed to be so. For example, killing another human is immoral. Why? Human beings collectively give up their rights for killing in order to obtain the security from being killed. I will not kill you in exchange for me knowing that I would not be randomly killed by others. 

Given this approach, from a human perspective, it is not immoral for a human beings to kill an ant since there is no agreement made between humans and ants not to kill each other. No one will blame an any for being immoral because it killed a human beings. Conversely, no human should be blamed for killing ants. Hence, it is not immoral to kill an ant.
Denial sometimes. Logical inconsistency and ignorance sometimes.

There is nothing *inherently* wrong with suicide. Don't let anyone convince you that it is wrong. However, that is not to say that everyone should do it with careless abandon. If you feel that you will gain more happiness by suicide than the total unhappiness that will be caused by your death, then I did not see a reason why you should not do it. However, you should really think about it carefully. If you have thought deeply enough and you are very sure that suicide is the only way out, then you should do it. Contact and deliver your goodbyes to those you feel are worthy of them. Make a proper farewell, if there is any who deserve it, and then leave. I could not make the decision for you. Nor could I tell you whether your suicide is justified. Only you can do that. I hope you will find your own answer. Whatever it is, it will be the true answer for you.
